messages:
elaine_cs: FYI, BrightCart (ticket BC-4128) — after the rollout this morning they say the model is now inventing price ranges for products (e.g. output includes "$12-$18" when only a single price $15 exists). Customer pasted a few examples below. Can we triage? :eyes:

BrightCart customer example:
```
User prompt: "Summarize the price for SKU:BC-987"
Model response (before rollout): "Price: $15"
Model response (after rollout): "Price: $12-$18 (estimated)"
```

marco_eng: thanks — can you get the API request IDs from the customer? we need one or two full request traces (request-id header or request_id from their app logs). also confirm which model they were pinned to and if they used any output_format or system messages.

elaine_cs: asked them to paste the request-id and the full prompt logs. I also sent them this snippet to retrieve logs from our support export endpoint (asked them to redact keys):
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer SUPPORT_TOKEN" \n  "https://api.redwood.inference/support/v1/requests/<REQUEST_ID>/prompt_log"
```
I told them to include: request_id, model name, region, and the exact request payload (headers + body) for 2-3 affected calls.

olga_research: quick checks — two likely causes: 1) a change in the post-processing / output-munging pipeline that inserts heuristics for pricing ranges; 2) a new guardrail/policy layer that attempts to be "helpful" by retrofitting ranges when price context is ambiguous. both would be outside the core model weights. do we have a recent change to the formatting helpers?

sam_ops: deploy-bot shows a canary rollout of serving-config v2.3.7 at 2026-03-14T03:12:00Z (rollout-id: r-5612). changelog note: "pricing-normalizer: add heuristic to emit 'estimated range' for sparse price signals" — copying that here. :thinking:

elaine_cs: okay — I told the customer we're investigating and requested the request_ids + minimal repro. they replied with one request id: rc_7f3a2b90 and said they used model "redwood/gpt-3o" pinned to region us-west-2. they also pasted the full user message (see above).

marco_eng: can you paste a minimal repro we can run locally? we need to reproduce with a single API call (no customer app logic). propose this template for the customer / for QA to use: 
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/gpt-3o",
  "input": "Summarize the price for SKU:BC-987",
  "max_tokens": 60,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "metadata": {"client_request_id": "test-minrepro-<you>"}
}
```
Also request the full response payload (including logprobs if available) and headers: X-Request-Id, X-Model-Version, X-Serving-Config.

olga_research: if you can capture the prompt log from our support endpoint that includes the system/profile templates we can see if a prefix was injected. the fact it emits a range (with words like "estimated") makes me suspect the pricing-normalizer was active.

sam_ops: I'm already rolling back the pricing-normalizer flag for r-5612 on canary. will ping once rollback finished.

deploy-bot: rollback of pricing-normalizer flag initiated for rollout r-5612 at 2026-03-14T04:02:10Z. status: in_progress.

elaine_cs: I'll follow up with the customer asking them to run the minimal repro and to paste the full response JSON for rc_7f3a2b90. I also asked them to include whether they used caching or prefix templates on their side.

marco_eng: once we have the prompt log we should check: exact system message, serving-config version header, and whether KV-cache prefixing happened (that could pump in a previous example that mentions ranges). if we reproduce, we can write a unit test and patch the post-process heuristic to only run when explicit price-range input present.

elaine_cs: customer just replied with two small repros (they ran the minimal repro):
```
1) request_id: rc_7f3a2b90 -> response: "Price: $12-$18 (estimated)"
2) request_id: rc_7f3a2f11 -> response: "Price: $15"
```
They also attached the prompt_log from support endpoint — I'll upload to the private incident room, linking eng.

marco_eng: great — if you can paste the serving headers and the prompt_log snippet here (no API keys) that's enough to start. especially need X-Serving-Config and any automated postprocess flags.

elaine_cs: uploaded prompt_log to #incidents-private (link omitted). prompt_log shows system template included: "You are a pricing assistant. When price is uncertain, provide an estimated range." — that matches the new heuristic. passes: we have a config bug.

marco_eng: thanks. filing a patch to disable the pricing-normalizer when input contains exact numeric price tokens. will ship hotfix to canary then prod once validated.

olga_research: also let's add a regression test to the eval harness using BrightCart's example prompts so we detect this in future rollouts.

elaine_cs: closing loop with customer: told them we've identified the pipeline heuristic, rolling back on canary, hotfix in progress, and will follow up in 2-3 hours with status. they appreciated the quick response. :thumbsup:

sam_ops: rollback complete on canary at 2026-03-14T04:05:46Z. monitoring for affected requests.

deploy-bot: rollback completed for r-5612 at 2026-03-14T04:05:46Z.

marco_eng: once canary is clean we'll patch mainline and run automated evals. thanks team.

elaine_cs: marking this thread resolved for now — will reopen if customer sees further regressions.
